guide.summary: Internal app in your own organization (self-serve, wait none); Public app, restricted scopes, server-side data (app review, wait several weeks to several months); Public app, sensitive or non-sensitive scopes only (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal app in your own organization (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app, restricted scopes, server-side data (app review, wait several weeks to several months).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed Gmail OAuth app for prototypes. For production, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret, using the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, no: Composio's managed Gmail app works. For launch, yes: you need your own app so users see your brand, you control scopes, and you get dedicated quota.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed default scopes may not include what you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Own app allows shorter trigger polling than the 15-minute managed minimum

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project and billing account
prerequisites.detail: You need a Cloud project to register the app. A billing account is needed to view or change usage limits or request a quota increase.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and verified website
prerequisites.detail: You need a privacy policy URL, and the domain must be verified in Search Console by a Project Owner or Editor.

steps.title: Create Cloud project and OAuth client
steps.detail: Register the app in Google Cloud console, pick the application type and create credentials.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Choose narrowest scopes
steps.detail: Map each needed feature to the least permissive Gmail scope and draft a justification for each.
steps.done_when: Scope list and justifications are drafted.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Enter app name, privacy policy, homepage and terms URLs, and the chosen scopes.
steps.done_when: Consent screen lists the same scopes as your app code.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Gmail auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into your Google OAuth client.
steps.done_when: Test connection completes with your app name shown.

steps.title: Verify domain in Search Console
steps.detail: Use an account that is Project Owner or Editor and a verified property owner.

steps.title: Submit verification request
steps.detail: Click Submit on the OAuth consent screen after reviewing the verification FAQ.

steps.title: Complete security assessment
steps.detail: Hire an approved assessor and remediate findings; an agent can help prepare evidence.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Google reviews the request; timing depends on data sensitivity.

traps.title: 100-user lifetime cap
traps.detail: Unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users over the project's lifetime and it cannot be reset.

traps.title: Scope or redirect changes trigger re-verification
traps.detail: Adding scopes, new redirect URLs or changing the product name after verification may require verification again.

traps.title: Scope mismatch shows unverified screen
traps.detail: If scopes in code differ from the consent screen, users see the unverified app screen.

traps.title: Site ownership blocks approval
traps.detail: Google will not approve verification until Search Console ownership is complete.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio name
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account', and quota is shared; switch before launch.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded the new-user authorization rate limit.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the grant rate on the OAuth consent screen page and request a quota increase.

blockers.what_it_means: The domain administrators disabled Gmail apps or have not trusted the app.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's domain admin to grant access via API Permissions in the Admin console.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft an instruction email for the admin.
